problem: Prior audio-visual navigation (the SoundSpaces AudioGoal task and methods such as Chen et al., Gan et al. and AV-WaN) assumes the target sounds continuously with a periodic signal. The sound source is placed at random with no visual embodiment or semantic context, so audio serves only as a positional beacon. These methods do not handle short, sporadic acoustic events, and they never learn to link sounds with visual objects or scene context.
motivation: Many real acoustic events are brief and tied to specific objects: a toilet flushing, a door creaking, a dishwasher chime. An agent must keep navigating after the sound stops, which requires inferring what object made the sound and where it probably is (for example, water dripping points to the bathroom). The authors extend SoundSpaces so that semantically meaningful sounds come from real Matterport3D object instances, which creates a task where audio-visual-semantic association is necessary.
key_idea: From binaural audio, infer an explicit goal descriptor made of the relative goal location and the object category. Aggregate it over time and carry it forward by odometry once the sound stops. Use it as the query of a transformer decoder that attends over a persistent multimodal (RGB-D + audio) scene memory, producing a goal-conditioned state for an RL policy.
insight: Most of the gain comes from the explicit goal descriptor, not from the transformer. Replacing the transformer with an RNN+MLP but keeping the goal descriptor network still beats Chen et al. (unheard: 21.4 vs 18.0 SR, 11.2 vs 6.9 SWS), and SMT+Audio, which has the same kind of memory but no descriptor, reaches only 16.7 SR. Within the descriptor, the spatial part matters more than the category part (Lt-only 23.9 SR vs Ct-only 20.5 SR vs full 24.8). Temporal aggregation raises category accuracy from 53.6% to 64.5%, lowers location error from 8.4 m to 8.1 m, and adds about 3 points of SR/SPL. 44% of successes end at a location different from the predicted Lt, meaning the agent relied on visual context for the predicted category, and injecting a random category drops SR/SPL by up to 8%. A ground-truth descriptor gives 65% SPL vs 24%, so goal inference from audio is the main bottleneck.
method: Semantic AudioGoal task/data: SoundSpaces on Matterport3D is extended with freesound.org clips for the 21 ObjectNav MP3D categories. Sounds are object-emitted or object-related, split into train/val/test clips, and rendered at real object instances. Event duration is sampled from N(15s, 9s), clipped to [5s, 500s]. Success requires stopping within 1 m of the specific sounding instance.

Observation encoder: RGB-D (64x64) and binaural spectrograms (2x65x26 per 1 s) are each encoded by a simplified ResNet-18 trained from scratch. These features are concatenated with pose (x, y, θ relative to start) and the previous action, then stored in a memory M of up to 150 steps.

Goal descriptor network: a CNN f_D(B_t) predicts the relative goal location (Δx, Δy), trained on-policy with MSE, and the object category, classified by a model pretrained off-policy on 3.5M spectrogram-category pairs and then frozen. Estimates are aggregated as D_t = 0.5·D̂_t + 0.5·f_p(D_{t-1}, Δp_t). When the sound stops, the descriptor is only transformed by the pose change.

Policy network: a transformer (1 encoder + 1 decoder layer, 8 heads, hidden size 256) self-attends over memory to get M_e. The decoder uses the goal descriptor D_t as query over M_e to produce state s_t, and linear actor and critic heads output the action distribution and value.

Training: DD-PPO in two stages. Stage 1 trains the encoder with memory size 1; stage 2 freezes the encoder and trains the rest with memory size 150. Rewards are +10 for success, ±1 for geodesic progress, and -0.01 per step. Training runs 300M steps with 150-step rollouts, Adam (lr 2.5e-4 policy, 1e-3 descriptor), on 0.5M training episodes.

setting.backbone: simplified ResNet-18 visual/audio encoders + 1-layer encoder/decoder transformer policy (hidden 256), all trained from scratch with DD-PPO
setting.training_data: 0.5M training episodes in SoundSpaces Matterport3D train scenes (85 MP3D envs total with train/val/test scene splits), 300M RL steps; category classifier pretrained on 3.5M spectrogram-category pairs from training environments; ~freesound.org object sound clips for 21 categories
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (center-cropped 64x64) + binaural audio (two 65x26 spectrograms per 1 s step) + agent pose relative to episode start + previous action
setting.action_space: discrete on SoundSpaces 1 m grid: MoveForward, TurnLeft, TurnRight, Stop (no actuation noise)
setting.privileged: noise-free pose (x, y, θ) relative to start and no actuation noise; in the distractor setting the one-hot target category is given to all models

numbers_note: The main-paper ablation table is captioned 'Table 3', but the text calls it Table 4; its 'Full model' row matches the unheard-sounds results. Cumulative success vs silence ratio is reported only in a figure (Fig. 4). Per-(goal, distractor) success rates appear in Supp. Table 5 and are not included here. Heard and unheard sounds are encoded in the benchmark name because this semantic AudioGoal task is distinct from the standard SoundSpaces AudioGoal task.
results: On the new semantic AudioGoal benchmark (SoundSpaces MP3D, 1,000 test episodes in unseen scenes), SAVi reaches 33.9 SR / 24.0 SPL / 21.5 SWS on heard sounds and 24.8 SR / 17.2 SPL / 14.7 SWS on unheard sounds. The strongest heard baseline is Gan et al. (29.3 / 23.7 / 14.4); on unheard sounds the best baselines are Chen et al. (18.0 SR / 13.4 SPL) and Gan et al. (8.0 SWS). SAVi also beats AV-WaN (heard 20.9 / 16.8) and SMT+Audio. With unheard distractor sounds, SAVi gets 11.8 SR / 7.4 SPL versus at most 4.2 SR / 2.9 SPL for baselines, though absolute performance is low for all methods.
limitations: Simulation only, with grid-based navigation (1 m nodes) and no actuation noise, because audio rendering exists only at grid points; there is no real-world test.

Goal inference from audio is weak: mean location error is 8.1 m and category accuracy 64.5%. The oracle descriptor gives 65% vs 24% SPL, and failures occur when the sound stops early or the agent stops prematurely near the target.
Performance collapses with distractor sounds (11.8 SR), and that setting requires the one-hot target category; there is no explicit source separation.
compares_to: Gan et al. (Look, listen, and act)
